composition.serve_who: This is a BUILDING/STRUCTURAL GA (Steering System GA, dwg 108-01-150-001) — perspective, plan, section, and detail views showing the twin-rudder steering mechanism installation: bearing structures, sheave boxes, tiller arms, rod links, autopilot ram, and wheel/track drive. It serves the established [150-rudder-blades] (rudder blade structure, already on register) and introduces the steering mechanism itself which belongs to [150-steering-system] (wheel/car/track/sheave/tiller drive train) and [150-autopilot-system] (autopilot ram and its support/mounting). BOM table (items 1-19) cross-references all balloons on the views. Structural facts (positions, dimensions, SWL-type data) attach to these nodes; no flow scenarios per class rules (mechanical linkage, not fluid/electrical schematic) — though the steering system's mechanical "flow" (wheel to rudder) is described qualitatively as a mechanism path per established facts, not a new scenario set.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The plan view, sections B-B/C-C, and details A/D/E/E all show the mechanical drive train from steering wheel input (implied via track/car item 11/13) through sheave boxes (items 8,9,10), Vectran line (14), rod link (15), to tiller arms (16,17) that rotate the rudder stocks. This is the steering mechanism proper, distinct from the rudder blades themselves and from the autopilot ram, matching node 150-steering-system.

functions.label: Wheel-to-rudder mechanical linkage (track/car/sheave/Vectran line/rod link/tiller arm)
functions.what_it_does: Converts helm wheel rotation (via track item 11 and assembled car item 13) into a pull on the Vectran line (item 14, 20mm) routed through upper and lower aluminium sheave boxes (items 8, 9) over 100mm aluminium sheaves (item 1) on sheave pin sets (item 10); the line motion is transferred through the carbon-tube rod link with BHD fittings and M16 ball joints (item 15) to the port and stbd assembled racing tiller arms (items 16, 17, 1400mm arm, 600/240 configuration) which rotate the rudder stocks. E-glass wedge stops (item 12) limit travel at the sheave box ends.

flow_scenarios.path: Track (11) + car (13) centered -> Vectran line (14) tension balanced through port and stbd sheave boxes (8,9) -> rod link (15) length set to 2044mm -> tiller arms (16,17) hold rudders at 1.8° toe-in (per established fact 150-rudder-blades)

Car (13) moves along track (11) -> pulls Vectran line (14) over sheaves (1) in upper/lower sheave boxes (8,9) -> rod link (15) transmits force via ball joints -> tiller arms (16,17) rotate rudder stocks -> E-glass wedge stops (12) arrest over-travel at the sheave box
Rod link (15) length varied 2025mm-2056mm -> toe-in angle at neutral varies 0° to 3° per table -> length set at build/commissioning, not adjustable underway

key_components: Rod link (mechanical push/pull linkage, length-adjustable for toe-in)

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Item 19 (autopilot ram, 300mm stroke) appears in plan and perspective views with a distinct callout 'AUTOPILOT RAM SUPPORT IS BOLTED THROUGH BHD L' and a separate penetration instruction in the tri-beam for pilot rod movement, indicating it is a separate actuation path from the manual wheel/tiller drive train (per established safety notes: 3 independent systems = 2 wheels + pilot).

functions.label: Autopilot ram actuation of rudder
functions.what_it_does: Provides powered rudder actuation independent of the two steering wheels, per the vessel's 3-independent-systems steering philosophy (established fact on 150-rudder-blades): 2 wheels + autopilot ram, each capable of controlling the rudders if the others fail.

flow_scenarios.path: Autopilot ram (19, 300mm stroke) extends/retracts -> pilot rod passes through penetration made in tri-beam (sized to suit pilot rod movement) -> acts on rudder linkage independently of wheel-driven Vectran/rod-link path
If both wheels fail, pilot ram remains in control of rudders (per 150-rudder-blades established fact); if a rod fails, one rudder remains active

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Rudder Blades (P+S, mirrored) — bearing/mounting hardware update
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: This sheet adds the bearing structure hardware (upper/lower bearing housings, water-tight neoprene tube, rudder retainer) that mount and seal each rudder stock, supplementing the already-established rudder blade facts (toe-in, Ackermann, 3-system safety) with the physical bearing/seal hardware positions.

functions.label: Rudder stock bearing and watertight seal assembly
functions.what_it_does: Supports and seals each rudder stock at two points (upper 180mm bearing, lower 220mm bearing) inside GRP bearing housings, with a neoprene watertight tube sealing the shaft penetration through the hull, retained by an aluminium rudder retainer at the top.

flow_scenarios.state: installed (per rudder, P and S mirrored)
flow_scenarios.path: Rudder stock -> 220mm bottom rudder bearing (item 2) in GRP housing (item 3) at hull bottom -> 180mm top rudder bearing (item 4) in GRP housing (item 5) at upper structure -> neoprene watertight tube (item 6, ⌀305mm) seals shaft through hull shell -> aluminium rudder retainer (item 7) caps/retains stock at top

infrastructure.system_name: Hull/structural framing at steering installation (tri-beams, bulkheads, partitions)
facts: Tri-beam 11, 6+7 provide structural support crossing the steering compartment; tri-beam 11 has a penetration made to suit pilot rod movement (autopilot ram clearance).
BHD L is the bulkhead through which the autopilot ram support is bolted, reinforced with bond tapping plates on its forward face.
Partition LM1 (port) and Partition LM2 (stbd) are bulkhead partitions adjacent to each rudder stock, hidden in Section B-B view.
STN 10 station line and DWL (design waterline) are structural/dimensional reference datums used throughout the plan and section views.

This is shared vessel structure (hull shell, bulkheads, tri-beams) supporting the steering system installation, not itself an item of equipment — no equipment node fits; retained as infrastructure context only.

uncertainties: Item BOM part numbers for several bearing/housing components (e.g., Solimar-00014986, 8038G220) are legible in the table but their supplier/manufacturer detail beyond 'Solimar' is not further specified on sheet — part number capture at inspection if ever needed, not a functional uncertainty.
Exact material/weight breakdown for items 15-17 (rod link, tiller arms) shows FRP/ALU(AG) material codes that are abbreviated on sheet; full material spec not decoded beyond what is legibly stated.

Whether the steering wheel/helm station itself (upstream of the track/car) is shown on this sheet is unclear — the track/car mechanism is shown but the wheel pedestal itself is not depicted in the extracted views; sheet may be cut off before the helm station.
